links.outcome: Surgical sensitivity (escalation recognition) versus specificity and over-triage in acute abdominal pain vignettes
links.effect: Surgical sensitivity 84.0% to 96.0% across models; specificity 64.0% to 80.0%; frequent over-triage decisions; positive likelihood ratios 2.33 to 4.60.
links.quote: Surgical sensitivity remained high across models (84.0% to 96.0%), whereas specificity was lower (64.0% to 80.0%) than specialist consensus.

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of frontier LLMs on synthetic clinical vignettes of acute abdominal pain to benchmark diagnostic sensitivity vs specificity and safety-stewardship trade-offs; does not evaluate a specific organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
